summary.name: VoiceInk
summary.one_liner: VoiceInk is a macOS dictation app that transcribes speech to text locally on the Mac and works across applications.
use_cases: dictating emails and notes on a Mac
writing prompts for AI tools by voice
transcribing meetings or updates into text
editing selected text by voice instruction
summary.what_it_does: VoiceInk uses local AI models to transcribe speech into text on the Mac, and the page says voice data stays on the device. It works in any application for writing, and it can remove filler words and repetition and format speech into emails, lists, or notes. Users can add custom words and names, and set replacements that expand short phrases. It can also rewrite selected text based on a spoken instruction, and save dictated notes with a timestamp to a Markdown journal. The page names Parakeet, WhisperKit, and Whisper among its models.
notable: Runs local AI transcription models with no voice data sent off the device; cloud enhancement is optional
Custom dictionary and saved replacements for names, product names, and short-phrase expansion
Open source, per the page and an awesome-mac listing
One-time purchase with lifetime updates and a 14-day refund; no subscription
caveats: Requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14.4 or later; Intel Macs are not supported
Paid license: $25 for 1 Mac, $39 for 2, $49 for 3
